title: Package Datasets
text: performing EPR experiments, especially X-band continuous wave (CW) spectroscopy solution, solvent plays important role. Namely, prior measurement one decide type cell applied depending solvent polarity. polar solvents, acetonitrile dimethyl sulfoxide, either capillary (\(.d. \leq 1\,\mathrm{mm}\) ) special quartz flat cell ( flat-part thickness \(\approx (0.3-0.6)\,\mathrm{mm}\)) must used. Whereas non-polar solvents, lower polarity, e.g. toluene, chloroform tetrahydrofuran, sample can analyzed within kind cell including common EPR quartz-tubes \(.d. \approx (2-4)\,\mathrm{mm}\). Additionally, solvent properties like melting/boiling point well viscosity essential variable temperature (VT) experiments particularly CW ENDOR well spectroelectrochemical ones. Table details can found ?solvents_ds documentation R file `data-raw` folder. Solvent properties can also obtained specialized readEPR_solvent_props() function.

title: Basic Functionality
text: Wuster’s reagent got name according C. title: Basic Functionality
text: Integration process analysis EPR spectra undoubtedly important operation mirrors amount paramagnetic centers/radicals within sample (see also quantify_EPR_Abs()). However, heavily dependent initial form EPR spectrum, .e. whether present either derivative (usually CW EPR) already integrated (usually 1D pulsed EPR) form/shape. Hence, spectrum integrated either twice , respectively. core-function used integration based cumulative trapezoidal approximation, available {pracma} 📦 pracma::cumtrapz() (10–13). relative error cumulative trapezoidal integration minimal, usually falling range \(\small \langle 1-5\rangle\,\%\) even lower depending spectrum resolution (11, 13). initial EPR spectrum displays low signal--noise ratio, integral required quantitative analysis looses sigmoid-shape ( see example shape). Therefore, case, best option simulate EPR spectrum evaluate integral spectrum (see e.g. quantify_EPR_Sim_series() function). big advantage method consists graphical representation corresponding integrals, .e. integration process may visually controlled manner like within EPR spectrometer acquisitions/processing software (see also plot_EPR_Specs_integ() function ). integration EPR spectral data essentially provided eval_integ_EPR_Spec() application experimental \(\small \ce{TMPD^{.+}}\) spectrum documented following scripts ➨ integrals, within entire \(\small B\)-range, can visualized plot_EPR_Specs_integ() function Visualization Graphics family: Figure 5.6: Single (single_Integ) double (sigmoid_Integ) integrated EPR spectrum \(\small \ce{TMPD^{.+}}\). Obviously, baseline single double integrated \(\small \ce{TMPD^{.+}}\) EPR spectrum somewhat distorted must corrected. fix baseline distortion, eval_integ_EPR_Spec() function contains corresponding arguments control baseline approximation, complex peak, polynomial fit provide subtraction single integrated spectrum evaluate double/sigmoid integral accurately ➨ Figure 5.7: Corrected single double integrated EPR spectrum \(\small \ce{TMPD^{.+}}\) (see also Figure 5.6). Maximum value double/sigmoid integral 0.0024 can used estimation \(\small \ce{TMPD^{.+}}\) amount within sample.
code: # basic integration without baseline correction # during the first integration. tmpd.data.norm.02.integ <-   eval_integ_EPR_Spec(     data.spectr = tmpd.data.norm.02,     B = "B_mT",     B.unit = "mT",     sigmoid.integ = TRUE   ) # # integration returns the original data frame # with the additional integrals  # `single_Integ` + `sigmoid_Integ` # # preview head(tmpd.data.norm.02.integ) #>       B_G   dIepr_over_dB    B_mT   single_Integ  sigmoid_Integ #> 1 3439.17 -4.38909680e-07 343.917 2.01424097e-06 0.00000000e+00 #> 2 3439.22 -2.38897973e-07 343.922 1.99729578e-06 1.00288419e-07 #> 3 3439.27 -3.01669413e-07 343.927 1.98378159e-06 1.99815353e-07 #> 4 3439.32  3.07043139e-10 343.932 1.97624753e-06 2.98816081e-07 #> 5 3439.37 -7.25313580e-07 343.937 1.95812237e-06 3.97175329e-07 #> 6 3439.42 -5.63170541e-07 343.942 1.92591027e-06 4.94276145e-07 # both integrals are presented separately # with their corresponding intensities automatically # scaled onto the `y`-axis (defined by "free_y") plot_EPR_Specs_integ(   tmpd.data.norm.02.integ,   slct.integs = c(     "single_Integ",     "sigmoid_Integ"   ),   B = "B_mT",   B.unit = "mT",   separate.integs = TRUE,   separate.integ.scales = "free_y" ) # correction of the TMPD^{.+} EPR spectrum single # integral by the 3rd degree polynomial tmpd.data.norm.02.integCorr <-   eval_integ_EPR_Spec(     data.spectr = tmpd.data.norm.02,     B = "B_mT",     B.unit = "mT",     correct.integ = TRUE,     # peak region to correct the baseline:     BpeaKlim = c(344.5, 355.5),     # polynomial degree to fit baseline      # under the peak region:     poly.degree = 3,     sigmoid.integ = TRUE   ) # # preview of both integrals (side-by-side), # data frame column of corrected integral # is denoted as `single_Integ_correct` plot_EPR_Specs_integ(   tmpd.data.norm.02.integCorr,   slct.integs = c(     "single_Integ_correct",     "sigmoid_Integ"   ),   B = "B_mT",   B.unit = "mT",   separate.integs = TRUE,   separate.integ.scales = "free_y" )

code: # decay of a triarylamine radical cation right after  # its generation by electrochemical potentiostatic oxidation  # in TBAPF6/CH3CN, double integrals (Areas) vs time were  # obtained by data pre-processing within the continuous  # wave (CW) EPR spectrometer acquisition/processing software. # # loading the built-in example file with the instrumental parameters triarylamine_rc_decay_dsc <-   load_data_example(file = "Triarylamine_radCat_decay_a.DSC") # # loading the built-in example file with "Area" vs "time" data frame triarylamine_rc_decay_txt <-   load_data_example(file = "Triarylamine_radCat_decay_a.txt") triarylamine_rc_decay_data <-   readEPR_Exp_Specs(     path_to_file = triarylamine_rc_decay_txt,     header = TRUE,     fill = TRUE,     select = c(3, 7),     col.names = c("time_s", "Area"),     x.unit = "s",     x.id = 1,     Intensity.id = 2,     qValue = 1700,     data.structure = "others"   ) %>% na.omit() # # fitting the experimental decay by 2R --> B kinetic model # with "k1" rate constant and the corresponding partial # rection order "alpha". "qvar0R" refers to the initial # "quantitative variable" (such as concentration, double integral # or number of radicals) of the triarylamine radical cation "R", # for a quick evaluation or comparison with other kinetic data # "qvarR" corresponds to "Area" (double integral in p.d.u. units)  # and therefore the unit => [k1] = (p.d.u.)^{-1} * s^{-1} # where the p.d.u. stands for "procedure defined unit" triarylamine_rc_decay_model <-   eval_kinR_EPR_modelFit(     data.qt.expr = triarylamine_rc_decay_data,     model.react = "(r=2)R --> [k1] B",     qvarR = "Area",     elementary.react = FALSE,     params.guess = c(       qvar0R = 0.019,       k1 = 0.04,       alpha = 1.9     ),     time.correct = TRUE,     path_to_dsc_par = triarylamine_rc_decay_dsc,     origin = "xenon"   ) # # graph preview triarylamine_rc_decay_model$plot # # data frame/table, showing the obtained kinetic parameters # (and their basic statistical measures) by the non-linear  # fit and numeric solution of the Ordinary Differential Equations triarylamine_rc_decay_model$df.coeffs #>           Estimate    Std. Error    t value       Pr(>|t|) #> qvar0R 0.018570037 5.7203136e-05 324.633198 4.3809413e-149 #> k1     0.060438055 5.4514583e-03  11.086585  6.1614969e-19 #> alpha  2.038206072 1.9676205e-02 103.587358 3.9216714e-101 # # graphical representation of the correlation matrix, # corresponding to kinetic model fit triarylamine_rc_decay_model$cor.df %>%    corrplot::corrplot(addCoef.col = "#c2c2c2")

Additionally"       #> [4] "supported by the Shapiro-Wilk test."        # ## compare the degrees of freedom with ## robust statistics by `MASS::fitdistr()` mass.pkg.fit.t <- MASS::fitdistr(   res.data.df$Residuals,   "t", ## Student's distro   lower = 1e-4 ) mass.pkg.fit.t$estimate[["df"]] #> [1] 5.550807 # ## generate data frame with residuals ## defined by the Normal/Gaussian distribution res.norm <- stats::rnorm(200,mean = 0,sd = 0.5) res.norm.data.df <- data.frame(Residuals = res.norm) # ## evaluate the `ABIC_forFit` by setting ## the `residuals.distro = "auto"` (default) list.norm.abic <- eval_ABIC_forFit(   data.fit = res.norm.data.df,   residuals = "Residuals",   k = 3 ## hypothetical number of model parameters ) # ## the entire list for the distribution fit list.norm.abic #> $abic.vec #> [1] 301.3228 314.3109 #>  #> $message #> [1] "Information criteria evaluated using the"    #> [2] "normal distribution of residuals,"           #> [3] "additionally supported by the Shapiro-Wilk"  #> [4] "as well as by the Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests." #>  # ## check, if the Student's t-distribution fit ## gives higher AIC/BIC + no clear support ## by the Kolmogorov-Smirnov ## and/or by the Shapiro-Wilk tests, ## the number of degrees of freedom (`df`) should be ## relatively high, because with such an extreme `df` ## Student's distro -> Normal/Gaussian one list.stud.abic <- eval_ABIC_forFit(   data.fit = res.norm.data.df,   residuals = "Residuals",   residuals.distro = "t-dist",   k = 3 ) list.stud.abic #> $abic.vec #> [1] 303.4228 319.6051 #>  #> $message #> [1] "Information criteria evaluated using the"   #> [2] "Student's t-distribution of residuals with" #> [3] "384894505.2 degrees of freedom. loading the kinetics: triarylamine.decay.series.data <-   readEPR_Exp_Specs_kin(     path_to_file = triarylamine.decay.series.bin.path,     path_to_dsc_par = triarylamine.decay.series.dsc.path,     path_to_ygf = triarylamine.decay.series.ygf.path    ) # ## select the first spectrum triarylamine.decay.series.data1st <-    triarylamine.decay.series.data$df %>%      dplyr::filter(time_s ==        triarylamine.decay.series.data$time[1]) # ## integrate the first spectrum with default arguments triarylamine.decay.data1st.integ01 <-   eval_integ_EPR_Spec(triarylamine.decay.series.data1st) # ## data frame preview head(triarylamine.decay.data1st.integ01) #>         B_G time_s  dIepr_over_dB      B_mT  single_Integ #> 1 3390.0000      6  1.3629316e-05 339.00000 1.0353596e-04 #> 2 3390.0833      6 -1.0134169e-06 339.00833 1.0406162e-04 #> 3 3390.1667      6 -1.9794802e-05 339.01667 1.0319461e-04 #> 4 3390.2500      6 -2.9826537e-05 339.02500 1.0112706e-04 #> 5 3390.3333      6 -1.6870754e-05 339.03333 9.9181337e-05 #> 6 3390.4167      6  2.5629187e-06 339.04167 9.8585177e-05 # ## integration (2nd integ.,including baseline correction) ## of the 1st spectrum from the series triarylamine.decay.data1st.integ02 <-   eval_integ_EPR_Spec(triarylamine.decay.series.data1st,     ## limits obtained from interactive spectrum:     BpeaKlim = c(3471.5,3512.5),     Blim = c(3425,3550),     correct.integ = TRUE,     poly.degree = 3,     sigmoid.integ = TRUE     ) # ## data frame preview head(triarylamine.decay.data1st.integ02) #> # A tibble: 6 × 8 #>     B_G time_s dIepr_over_dB  B_mT single_Integ baseline_Integ_fit #>   <dbl>  <dbl>         <dbl> <dbl>        <dbl>              <dbl> #> 1 3425.      6   -0.0000160   343.    0.0000326          0.0000227 #> 2 3425.      6   -0.00000338  343.    0.0000317          0.0000227 #> 3 3425.      6    0.0000173   343.    0.0000323          0.0000227 #> 4 3425.      6    0.0000157   343.    0.0000337          0.0000226 #> 5 3425.      6   -0.0000271   343.    0.0000332          0.0000226 #> 6 3425.      6    0.00000128  343.    0.0000322          0.0000226 #> # ℹ 2 more variables: single_Integ_correct <dbl>, sigmoid_Integ <dbl> # ## plot the single integrated EPR spectrum, ## including baseline correction plot_EPR_Specs(triarylamine.decay.data1st.integ02,                x = "B_G",                x.unit = "G",                Intensity = "single_Integ_correct",                lineSpecs.form = "integrated"              )  # ## plot, corresponding to double/sigmoid integral, ## which is related to corrected single integral plot_EPR_Specs(triarylamine.decay.data1st.integ02,                x = "B_G",                x.unit = "G",                Intensity = "sigmoid_Integ",                lineSpecs.form = "integrated"              )  # ## vectorized output of the uncorrected `sigmoid_integral` triarylamine.decay.data1st.integ03 <-   eval_integ_EPR_Spec(triarylamine.decay.series.data1st,                       sigmoid.integ = TRUE,                       vectorize = TRUE)[["sigmoid"]] # ## preview of the first 6 values triarylamine.decay.data1st.integ03[1:6] #> [1] 0.0000000e+00 8.6498993e-06 1.7285576e-05 2.5798979e-05 3.4145162e-05 #> [6] 4.2385433e-05 # ## incorporation of vectorized integration into ## data "pipe" ("%>%") `dplyr` processing of EPR spectral ## time series, creating column with `sigmoid` integral ## where its corresponding single integral (intensity) ## has undergone a baseline correction, finally the max. value ## of all sigmoid integrals along with the time is ## summarized in data frame for quantitative kinetic analysis triarylamine.decay.data.integs <-   triarylamine.decay.series.data$df %>%   dplyr::group_by(time_s) %>%   dplyr::filter(dplyr::between(B_G,3425,3550)) %>%   dplyr::mutate(sigmoid_Integ =     eval_integ_EPR_Spec(dplyr::pick(B_G,dIepr_over_dB),                         correct.integ = TRUE,                         BpeaKlim = c(3471.5,3512.5),                         poly.degree = 3,                         sigmoid.integ = TRUE,                         vectorize = TRUE)$sigmoid                        ) %>%   dplyr::summarize(Area = max(sigmoid_Integ)) ## in such case `Blim` range is not defined by ## the `eval_integ_EPR_Spec`, however the `Blim = NULL` ## as well as the `dplyr::between()` must be set !!! # ## preview of the final data frame head(triarylamine.decay.data.integs) #> # A tibble: 6 × 2 #>   time_s   Area #>    <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1      6 0.0169 #> 2     21 0.0179 #> 3     36 0.0169 #> 4     51 0.0172 #> 5     66 0.0184 #> 6     81 0.0158 # ## preview of the simple plot ggplot2::ggplot(triarylamine.decay.data.integs) +   ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(x = time_s,y = Area))  # ## this does not correspond to example ## in `eval_kinR_EPR_modelFit`, `eval_kin_EPR_ODE_model` ## or in `plot_theme_NoY_ticks` based on the same input data, ## as those `Area` vs `time` relations were evaluated using ## the simulated EPR spectra (see also `vignette("datasets")`) # if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Similar to previous data processing, creating both: corrected ## single integral + sigmoid integral for each time within the spectral ## series. Sigmoid integral was evalutated from the single one by ## `cumtrapz()` function from `pracma` package and finally re-scaled. triarylamine.decay.data.integs <-   triarylamine.decay.series.data$df %>%   dplyr::group_by(time_s) %>%   eval_integ_EPR_Spec(correct.integ = TRUE,                       Blim = c(3425,3550),                       BpeaKlim = c(3472.417,3505.5),                       poly.degree = 3) %>%  dplyr::group_by(time_s) %>%  dplyr::mutate(sigmoid_Integ =    pracma::cumtrapz(B_G,single_Integ_correct)[,1]) %>%  dplyr::mutate(sigmoid_Integ_correct =    abs(min(sigmoid_Integ) - sigmoid_Integ)) } # } # ## integral of the PNT EPR spectrum in integrated form, ## first generate the simulated spectrum/data pnt.sim.integ.iso <-   eval_sim_EPR_iso(g.iso = 2.0027,     instrum.params = c(Bcf = 3500, # central field                        Bsw = 100, # sweep width                        Npoints = 4096,                        mwGHz = 9.8), # MW Freq. in GHz     B.unit = "G",     nuclear.system = list(       list("1H",3,5.09), # 3 x A(1H) = 5.09 MHz       list("1H",6,17.67) # 6 x A(1H) = 17.67 MHz      ),     lineSpecs.form = "integrated",     lineGL.DeltaB = list(0.54,NULL), # Gauss. FWHM in G     Intensity.sim = "Integ_Intensity"   ) ## data frame preview head(pnt.sim.integ.iso$df) #>     Bsim_G  Bsim_mT    Bsim_T Integ_Intensity #> 1 3450.000 345.0000 0.3450000               0 #> 2 3450.024 345.0024 0.3450024               0 #> 3 3450.049 345.0049 0.3450049               0 #> 4 3450.073 345.0073 0.3450073               0 #> 5 3450.098 345.0098 0.3450098               0 #> 6 3450.122 345.0122 0.3450122               0 # ## integrated EPR spectrum preview pnt.sim.integ.iso$plot  # ## no integration in case of integrated `lineSpecs.form` ## if `sigmoid.integ = FALSE` intens.integ.NOcorrect.df <-   eval_integ_EPR_Spec(     data.spectr = pnt.sim.integ.iso$df,     B = "Bsim_G",     Intensity = "Integ_Intensity",     lineSpecs.form = "integrated"  ) #> Warning:  If `sigmoid.integ = FALSE` the EPR spectrum won't be integrated, #>  #>               only the baseline correction can be performed. #>  #>               In order to evaluate the corresponding integral, please assign #>  #>               `sigmoid.integ = TRUE` !  ## data frame preview head(intens.integ.NOcorrect.df) #>     Bsim_G  Bsim_mT    Bsim_T Integ_Intensity #> 1 3450.000 345.0000 0.3450000               0 #> 2 3450.024 345.0024 0.3450024               0 #> 3 3450.049 345.0049 0.3450049               0 #> 4 3450.073 345.0073 0.3450073               0 #> 5 3450.098 345.0098 0.3450098               0 #> 6 3450.122 345.0122 0.3450122               0 # ## in order to obtain sigmoid integral, ## assign `sigmoid.integ = TRUE` sigmoid.integral.df <-   eval_integ_EPR_Spec(     data.spectr = pnt.sim.integ.iso$df,     B = "Bsim_G",     Intensity = "Integ_Intensity",     lineSpecs.form = "integrated",     sigmoid.integ = TRUE   ) ## data frame preview head(sigmoid.integral.df) #>     Bsim_G  Bsim_mT    Bsim_T Integ_Intensity sigmoid_Integ #> 1 3450.000 345.0000 0.3450000               0             0 #> 2 3450.024 345.0024 0.3450024               0             0 #> 3 3450.049 345.0049 0.3450049               0             0 #> 4 3450.073 345.0073 0.3450073               0             0 #> 5 3450.098 345.0098 0.3450098               0             0 #> 6 3450.122 345.0122 0.3450122               0             0 # ## plot previous integral plot_EPR_Specs(   sigmoid.integral.df,   x = "Bsim_G",   x.unit = "G",   Intensity = "sigmoid_Integ",   lineSpecs.form = "integrated" )

text: data.vec.col Numeric vector (pointing column) interest (within data frame) calculate confidence interval uncertainty (margin error). level.cnfd Numeric (floating) value, corresponding confidence level (default: level.cnfd = 0.95). value related significance level \(alpha\) defined \(1 - confidence\,\,level\). separate Logical, whether separate mean value uncertainty (margin error), corresponding non-negative right/left confidence limit mean. separate = TRUE (default), result shown named vector (mean) value uncertaity. Otherwise, result returned format \(value\pm\,\,uncertainty\).

title: Confidence Interval of a Vector or Data Frame Column — eval_interval_cnfd_tVec
text: confidence interval evaluation suggests two-tailed Student's t-distribution,   number observations \(N > 30\) approaches normal \(z\)-distribution.   Evaluation confidence interval /limits can well documented \(g\)-factor series example:   $$g = \overline{g}\pm (t_{(1-\alpha/2),df}\,s/\sqrt{N})$$   \(\overline{g}\) mean value \(t_{(1-\alpha/2),df}\) corresponds quantile   t-distribution significance level \(\alpha\) (\(1-\alpha = condfidence\,\,level\),   see level.cnfd argument) degrees freedom \(df = N -1\). Finally, \(s\) represents   sample standard deviation, defined following relation (regarding \(g\)-value series example):   $$s = \sqrt{(1/(N-1))\,\sum_{=1}^N (g_i - \overline{g})^2}$$   computed sd function. -mentioned \(t\)-quantile actually calculated   stats::qt. Alternatively, one also evaluate confidence   interval one sample t.test certain level confidence, giving descriptive output   statistical characteristics.

text: data.qt.expr data frame object, containing concentrations/integral intensities/areas EPR spectra calculated using experimental data well time column. two essential columns described character strings like (see arguments time qvarR). time.unit Character string, corresponding time unit like "s" (default), "min" (minutes), "h" (hours) "ms" (milliseconds). time Character string, pointing time column/variable name original data.qt.expr data frame. Default: time = "time_s". qvarR Character string, pointing qvarR (quantitative variable related radical) column/variable name original data.qt.expr. Default: qvarR = "Area". model.react Character string, denoting specific radical ("R") reaction related changes integral intensities (quantitative variable) EPR spectral time series. Arrow shows direction reaction ("-->", forward "<==>", forward + reverse). Rate constants indicated square brackets arrows. Following examples reaction schemes predefined commonly used describe integral intensity /radical concentration/amount changes EPR time series experiment (r,,b stoichiometric coefficients may vary, see ). Couple examples also given Details. function relatively flexible enables later addition reaction schemes describing EPR time series experiments (MAY ASK DEVELOPER(S) via forum/help-channels). stoichiometric coefficient ((r=1) (=1)) can varied within model.react character string. Defined/Allowed values integers, e.g. 1,2,3...etc. space character within model.react string fixed can skipped sake simplicity. elementary.react = FALSE (model reaction considered elementary one), possible non-integer partial coefficients (e.g. alpha,beta gamma) must included kin.params (see also kin.params description). consecutive model reaction presented , applies one part/step mechanism. elementary.react Logical, model reaction considered elementary one, .e. stoichiometric coefficients equal partial reaction orders. reaction proceeds without identifiable intermediate species forming. Default: elementary.react = TRUE. elementary.react = FALSE, .e. model.react considered like elementary one, user must include parameterized reaction orders \(\alpha\), \(\beta\) \(\gamma\) kin.params, e.g kin.params = c(k1 = 0.01, qvar0A = 0.05, alpha = 1.5). consecutive model reaction presented , applies one part/step mechanism. params.guess Named vector, initial values kin.params (see eval_kinR_ODE_model) ready optimization/fitting. k1-unit eventually expressed terms \(s^{-1}\) well units applied qvar (e.g. c, concentration) depends partial reaction order(s), power(s) qvar(s). example, k1-unit elementary radical recombination, evaluated double integrals, like model.react = "(r=2)R --> [k1] B", reads: \(\text{s}^{-1}\,(\text{p.d.u.})^{-1}\). params.guess.lower Numeric vector lower bounds parameter params.guess. given, default (params.guess.lower = NULL) lower bound corresponds -Inf params.guess component. params.guess.upper Numeric vector upper bounds parameter params.guess. given, default (params.guess.upper = NULL) upper bound corresponds +Inf params.guess component. fit.kin.method Character string, pointing optimization/fitting method. far, default one (fit.kin.method = "diff-levenmarq") exclusively used (additional methods planned). corresponds differential Levenberg-Marquardt (see also nls.lm) based numeric solution ordinary differential equations common integration rate equations. solve.ode.method Character string, setting integrator (method argument ode), applied find numeric solution ODE. Default: solve.ode.method = "lsoda" (lsoda, additional methods (e.g. "rk4", "daspk", "euler"), see link ode function ). time.frame.model Numeric value, corresponding interval time resolution, .e. smallest time difference two consecutive points time.unit. Therefore, number points defined time.interval.model argument: $$((Interval[2] - Interval[1])\,/\,Frame) + 1$$ \(Interval[2]\), \(Interval[1]\) equal 2nd 1st element time.interval.model, respectively; \(Frame\) corresponds time.frame.model. argument required numerically solve kinetic differential equations ode. default interval mentioned , default value reads time.frame.model = 2 (time.unit). time.correct Logical, time recorded series EPR spectra needs corrected. Default: time.correc = FALSE, actually assumes time correction done (either correct_time_Exp_Specs readEPR_Exp_Specs_kin subsequent integration), prior fitting procedure. time.correct = TRUE, path file EPR instrumental parameters (like .DSC/.dsc par) must defined (see path_to_dsc_par). path_to_dsc_par Character string, path (also provided file.path) .DSC/.dsc .par (depending origin parameter) text files including instrumental parameters provided EPR machine. corresponding data (double integrated ## EPR spectrum = `Area` vs `time`) triaryl_radCat_data <-   readEPR_Exp_Specs(triaryl_radCat_path,                     header = TRUE,                     fill = TRUE,                     select = c(3,7),                     col.names = c("time_s","Area"),                     x.unit = "s",                     x.id = 1,                     Intensity.id = 2,                     qValue = 1700,                     data.structure = "others") %>%   na.omit() ## data preview head(triaryl_radCat_data) #>   time_s        Area #> 1   0.00 0.018741176 #> 2  15.17 0.018117647 #> 3  30.01 0.017617647 #> 4  44.82 0.017194118 #> 5  59.66 0.016511765 #> 6  74.52 0.016347059 # ## half-life (t1/2) of the second-order from data frame ## search for the value/point which is close to 0.08/2 t.half.01.a.idx <- which.min(abs(kin.test.01$df$R - 0.04)) t.half.01.a <- kin.test.01$df[t.half.01.a.idx,] %>%   dplyr::pull(time) # ## theoretical (analytical) expression of half-life t.half.01.b <- 1 / (2 * 0.08 * 0.012) # ## comparison of both values t.half.01.a #> [1] 520 t.half.01.b #> [1] 520.83333 # ## plot kinetic model profile with t1/2 kin.test.01$plot +   ggplot2::geom_hline(     yintercept = 0.08/2,     linetype = "dashed",     color = "blue"   ) + ggplot2::geom_vline(     xintercept = t.half.01.a,     linetype = "dashed",     color = "blue"   ) + ggplot2::annotate(     geom = "text",     x = 640,     y = 0.045,     color = "blue",     size = 5.4,     label = "italic(t)[1/2]",     parse = TRUE   )  # ## consecutive reactions and the corresponding plot ## (`model.react` character string without spaces) kin.test.02 <-  eval_kinR_ODE_model(    model.react = "(a=2)A<==>[k1][k4](r=2)R<==>[k2][k3](b=1)B",    kin.params = c(k1 = 0.225,                   k2 = 0.1,                   k3 = 2e-4,                   k4 = 2e-5,                   qvar0A = 0.02,                   qvar0R = 0.002,                   qvar0B = 0)  ) ## plot preview kin.test.02$plot  # ## data frame/table preview head(kin.test.02$df) #>   time           A            R             B #> 1    0 0.020000000 0.0020000000 0.0000000e+00 #> 2    2 0.019646311 0.0023517836 9.5289887e-07 #> 3    4 0.019304915 0.0026906259 2.2293018e-06 #> 4    6 0.018975184 0.0030170909 3.8623200e-06 #> 5    8 0.018656601 0.0033316443 5.8771481e-06 #> 6   10 0.018348515 0.0036348779 8.3036200e-06 # ## loading example data (incl. `Area` and `time` variables) ## from Xenon software: decay of a triarylamine radical cation ## after its generation by electrochemical oxidation triaryl_radCat_path <-   load_data_example(file = "Triarylamine_radCat_decay_a.txt") ## corresponding data (double integrated ## EPR spectrum = `Area` vs `time`) triaryl_radCat_data <-   readEPR_Exp_Specs(     triaryl_radCat_path,     header = TRUE,     fill = TRUE,     select = c(3,7),     col.names = c("time_s","Area"),     x.unit = "s",     x.id = 1,     Intensity.id = 2,     qValue = 1700,     data.structure = "others") %>%   na.omit() ## data preview head(triaryl_radCat_data) #>   time_s        Area #> 1   0.00 0.018741176 #> 2  15.17 0.018117647 #> 3  30.01 0.017617647 #> 4  44.82 0.017194118 #> 5  59.66 0.016511765 #> 6  74.52 0.016347059 # ## comparison of the kinetic model with the experimental ## data `triaryl_radCat_data`, kinetic parameters were estimated ## to be as close as possible to the latter. compar_model_expr_data_01 <-   eval_kinR_ODE_model(     model.react = "(r=2)R --> [k1] B",     kin.params = c(qvar0R = 0.019,                    k1 = 0.04),     time.interval.model = c(0,1500),     data.qt.expr = triaryl_radCat_data,     qvar.expr = "Area",     time.expr = "time_s"    ) ## text: frequency MHz calculated according relation   $$\nu_{\text{ENDOR}}^{} = - (1/h)\,\mu_{\text{N}}^{}\,g_{\text{n}}^{}\,B\,10^{-6}$$   \(h\) Planck's constant, \(\mu_{\text{N}}^{}\) nuclear magneton   available constants package (constants::syms$mun),   \(g_{\text{n}}^{}\) nuclear \(g\)-factor specific nucleus (reported package   isotopes_ds data frame g_Nuclear) finally, \(B\) denotes magnetic flux   density ENDOR spectra recorded (see also B.val arguments). \(10^{-6}\) coefficient   referred resulting frequency MHz. negative sign "\(-\)" mirrors convention describe direction   magnetic spin moments precession either counter-clockwise (\(+\), \(\gamma_{\text{n}}^{} < 0\))   clockwise (\(-\), \(\gamma_{\text{n}}^{} > 0\), Levitt MH (2013)).

text: General-purpose optimization objective fn function (also called "fitness")   minimized order fit theoretical models (EPR simulations)   onto experimental data. Several methods/algorithms implemented (see also Details):   nloptr package: slsqp,   neldermead, crs2lm, sbplx,   cobyla, lbfgs;   minpack.lm package:   nls.lm finally   pso package:   psoptim.

title: General Function for Non-Linear Optimization/Fitting of EPR Parameters/Data — optim_for_EPR_fitness
text: method Character string, pointing applied optimization method/algorithm. One may choose one listed Details, default: method = "neldermead", setting "Nelder-Mead" simplex method. x.0 Numeric vector initial values optimized order fit onto experimental data. fn Objective function minimized. Usually function calculating sum residual squares, general parameterized one can implemented (see Details Examples). lower, upper lower upper bound constraints. data Data frame object, containing columns/variables (e.g. intensity EPR spectrum), required undergo fitting/optimization process. Nmax.evals Numeric value, maximum number function evaluations /iterations. one method, limited argument, nls.lm, Nmax.evals = 1024. Higher Nmax.evals may extremely extend optimization time, therefore default value reads Nmax.evals = 512. However, "pswarm" method requires least default even higher values. tol.step Numeric, smallest optimization step (relative change) 2 iterations stop optimization procedure. method = "pswarm" (particle swarm optimization procedure) actually corresponds tolerance restarting. maximum distance "best" particle others less tol.step * pswarm.diameter) algorithm restarts. See also psoptim. Default: tol.step = 5e-7. pswarm.size Numeric value, equals particle swarm size (.e. number particles), method = "pswarm". default value (pswarm.size = NULL) actually corresponds floor(10+2*sqrt(length(Np))) (SPSO2007, see pswarm.type argument), e.g. optimize 8 parameters, number particles = 15. length(Np) corresponds either length(x.0) difference length(x.0) number parameters, (upper - lower) == 0 (.e. x.0 parameters actually fixed/optimized). SPSO2011 default number particles equals 40. pswarm.diameter Numeric value, corresponding diameter particle swarm search space (case method = "pswarm"). default value (pswarm.diameter = NULL) refers Euclidean distance, defined : $$\sqrt{\sum_k\,(\text{upper}[k] - \text{lower}[k])^2}$$ pswarm.type Character string, setting type/version particle swarm algorithm method = "pswarm". two types available: pswarm.type = "SPSO2007" pswarm.type = "SPSO2011". latter introduced adaptive random topology, allows swarm dynamically adjust communication structure. helps maintaining diversity swarm improves algorithm's ability escape local optima. type generally offers better performance larger multidimensional spaces pswarm.type = "SPSO2007", uses static topology. Details may found References. Default: pswarm.type = NULL (actually corresponding "SPSO2007", performs slightly better smaller scales common simulations EPR spectra lower number parameters like hyperfine coupling constants). eval.optim.progress Logical. TRUE progress optimization/fitting, defined method argument, monitored/tracked R console. default value set FALSE higher number evaluations/iterations might result several tens hundreds rows information, depending applied method. case {nloptr} methods/functions well method = "pswarm" displays iteration number (10-th iteration per particle shown pswarm) value objective/fitness function (e.g. least-square minimization RSS). Additionally, pswarm method shows possible shrinking particle swarm diameter convergence. method = "levenmarq" shows iteration/evaluation number, sum residual squares (RSS) relevant parameter (Par.) value. eval_sim_EPR_isoFit quantify_EPR_Sim_series argument can combined msg.optim.progress. fix.optim.x.0.id Numeric value/vector x.0 indices, corresponding x.0 elements fixed optimization/fitting, .e. optimized lower upper limits equal related elements initial x.0. example, 1st 3rd parameter/element x.0 supposed fixed, put fix.optim.x.0.id = c(1,3). Default: fix.optim.x.0.id = NULL, .e. none x.0 elements fixed parameters optimized required (see also eval_sim_EPR_isoFit). However, even case fix.optim.x.0.id = NULL, parameters can fixed adjustment corresponding lower upper arguments. ... additional arguments passed function.

title: General Function for Non-Linear Optimization/Fitting of EPR Parameters/Data — optim_for_EPR_fitness
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## following code snippets were taken from ## the `quantify_EPR_Sim_series` function # ## if an EPR spectrum consists of several ## components or several radical spectra partly overlay, ## following simple function, taking the linear ## combination of max. 6 EPR simulated intensities, ## can be applied in order to fit the sum of the individual ## simulations onto the experimental EPR spectrum ## envelope, the input parameters therefore correspond ## to zero-point/intercept(par[1]) and coefficients ## of the linear combinations(par[2]...par[7]), ## equal to individual intensity multiplications: fit_params_specs_par <- function(data,                                  col.name.pattern,                                  par){   #   # data contains variables/columns of simulated   # intensities with the headers characterized   # by the `col.name.patter`   #   data <- data[,grep(col.name.pattern,                      colnames(data),                      value = TRUE)]   #   ## create a sum for all columns/simulated spectra   if (ncol(data) == 1){     summa <- par[1] + (par[2] * data[[1]])   }   if (ncol(data) == 2){       summa <- par[1] + (par[2] * data[[1]]) +       (par[3] * data[[2]])   }   if (ncol(data) == 3){     summa <- par[1] + (par[2] * data[[1]]) +       (par[3] * data[[2]]) +       (par[4] * data[[3]])   }   if (ncol(data) == 4){     summa <- par[1] + (par[2] * data[[1]]) +       (par[3] * data[[2]]) +       (par[4] * data[[3]]) +       (par[5] * data[[4]])   }   if (ncol(data) == 5){     summa <- par[1] + (par[2] * data[[1]]) +       (par[3] * data[[2]]) +       (par[4] * data[[3]]) +       (par[5] * data[[4]]) +       (par[6] * data[[5]])   }   if (ncol(data) == 6){     summa <- par[1] + (par[2] * data[[1]]) +       (par[3] * data[[2]]) +       (par[4] * data[[3]]) +       (par[5] * data[[4]]) +       (par[6] * data[[5]]) +       (par[7] * data[[6]])   }   #  return(summa)  }  #  ## following function is applied to vary only  ## `method`, `function` and `data` optim_fn <- function(fun,method,data){   optim.list <-     optim_for_EPR_fitness(x.0 = optim.params.init,                           method = method,                           fn = fun,                           lower = optim.params.lower,                           upper = optim.params.upper,                           Nmax.evals = Nmax.evals,                           tol.step = tol.step,                           pswarm.size = pswarm.size,                           pswarm.diameter = pswarm.diameter,                           data = data,                           col.name.pattern =                           "Sim.*_[[:upper:]]$"     )   #   return(optim.list)  } # ## finally, the following function is to be minimized: min_residuals_ps <- function(data,col.name.pattern,par){   sum((data[[Intensity.expr]] -     fit_params_specs_par(data,col.name.pattern,par))^2)   } # ## therefore, the final `optimization` list may look like optimization.list <-   lapply(seq(data.list),          function(o) {          optim_fn(method = optim.method,          data = data.list[[o]],          fun = min_residuals_ps)        }     ) ## where `data.list` represents the list of data frames ## including all individual simulated spectra ## (one data frame for each spectrum + original ## experimental spectrum intensity column) # } # }

Default: x = "E_V" (potential volts). x.unit Character string, pointing x-quantity unit. following units available: x.unit = "V", x.unit = "mV" (case voltammetry, x corresponds potential) well x.unit = "s", x.unit = "ms" x.unit = "min" (case chronoamperometry, x corresponds time). Default: x.unit = "V". Current Character string, indicating Current(\(\))-axis/column quantity original data.vat object. Default: Current = "I_ua" (current \(\text{µA}\)). Current.unit Character string, pointing Current quantity unit like Current.unit = "uA" (microamps, default), Current.unit = "", Current.unit = "mA" Current.unit = "nA". xlim Numeric vector x-quantity lower upper visual limit, e.g. xlim = c(-100,400) (potential "mV", case voltammetry) xlim = c(0,1000) (time seconds, case chronoamperometry). Default: xlim = NULL actually setting entire x-range original dataset. Ilim Numeric vector, characterizing lower upper visualization limit current, e.g. Ilim = c(-0.05,0.2), corresponding current milliamps. Default: Ilim = NULL related entire current (\(\)) range original dataset. line.color Character string, pointing line color voltammogram / chronoamperogram. {ggplot2} compatible colors allowed, e.g. line.color = "blue". simple plot of an EPR spectrum with B in `mT` ## and dIepr_over_dB_Sim in `p.d.u.` (derivative intensity) plot_EPR_Specs(aminoxyl.data)  # ## the same spectrum with B in `G` and `theme_bw` ## ggplot2 graph theme plot_EPR_Specs(data.spectra = aminoxyl.data,                x = "B_G",                x.unit = "G",                theme.basic = "theme_bw")  # ## the same spectrum in g-scale and without ## panel background plot_EPR_Specs(   data.spectra = aminoxyl.data,   x = "g_value",   x.unit = "unitless",   xlim = c(1.95,2.075) ) + ggplot2::theme(   panel.background = ggplot2::element_blank() )  # ## single integration (without baseline correction) ## of the previous spectrum by the `eval_integ_EPR_Spec` ## function aminoxyl.data.sinteg <-   eval_integ_EPR_Spec(aminoxyl.data) ## plot the single integrated spectrum plot_EPR_Specs(aminoxyl.data.sinteg,                x = "B_G",                x.unit = "G",                Intensity = "single_Integ",                line.colors = "darkorange",                line.type = "dashed",                lineSpecs.form = "integrated")  # ## loading the built-in CW ENDOR spectrum ## of perinaphthenyl (PNT) pnt.bin.file.path <- load_data_example("PNT_ENDOR_a.DTA") pnt.pars.file.path <- load_data_example("PNT_ENDOR_a.DSC") ## read the PNT CW ENDOR data without intensity ## normalization pnt.endor.data <-   readEPR_Exp_Specs(     path_to_file = pnt.bin.file.path,     path_to_dsc_par = pnt.pars.file.path,     col.names = c("index",                   "RF_MHz",                   "dIepr_over_dB"),     x.unit = "MHz") ## plotting the previous ENDOR data spectrum ## in derivative form with `darkred` linecolor ## and 1.2 mm linewidth: plot_EPR_Specs(pnt.endor.data,                x = "RF_MHz",                x.unit = "MHz",                line.colors = "darkred",                line.width = 1.2)  # ## loading the built-in package example to demonstrate ## visualizatioin of time series EPR spectra: triarylamine.decay.series.dsc.path <- load_data_example(file =         "Triarylamine_radCat_decay_series.DSC") triarylamine.decay.series.bin.path <- load_data_example(file =         "Triarylamine_radCat_decay_series.DTA") ## loading the kinetics: triarylamine.decay.series.data <-   readEPR_Exp_Specs_kin(     path_to_file =       triarylamine.decay.series.bin.path,     path_to_dsc_par =       triarylamine.decay.series.dsc.path    ) # ## plot with the CONTINUOUS COLORSCALE (see argument ## `line.colors` and color definitions `1.`): plot_EPR_Specs(triarylamine.decay.series.data$df,                var2nd.series = "time_s",                line.colors =                grDevices::hcl.colors(8,palette = "Roma"),                legend.title = "Time (s)",                yTicks = FALSE)  # ## plot with the DISCRETE COLORSCALE (see argument ## `line.colors` and color definitions `2.`), ## each 10-th spectrum from the original plot is presented: plot_EPR_Specs(triarylamine.decay.series.data$df,                var2nd.series = "time_s",                var2nd.series.slct.by = 10,                line.colors = c("darkblue",                                "darkorange",                                "darkviolet"),                legend.title = "Time (s)")  # if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## display the variable temperature experiment selecting ## the DISCRETE COLORSCALE where all EPR spectra from ## the series are presented: plot_EPR_Specs(data.spectra,   Ilim = c(-4e-3,4e-3),   var2nd.series = "T_K", # temperature in Kelvins   var2nd.series.slct.by = 1,   line.colors = c("darkblue",                   "darkorange",                   "magenta",                   "steelblue"),   legend.title = "Temperature (K)") } # }

B.unit Character string, pointing unit magnetic flux density (coming original datasets) presented \(B\)-axis EPR spectrum. Strings like "G" (`Gauss`) (default) "mT" (`millitesla`) can used. Blim Numeric vector, magnetic flux density mT/G corresponding lower upper visual limit selected \(B\)-region, Blim = c(3495.4,3595.4). Intensity.shift.ratio Numeric (0), showing 'far' simulated EPR spectrum presented underneath experimental one. lower ratio, 'deeper' simulated spectrum offset, default: Intensity.shift.ratio = 1.2, common values : 0.6,0.8, 1.2,1.1. Intensity.shift.ratio = NULL, SPECTRA PRESENTED OVERLAY MODE ! B.shift Numeric, difference \(B_{center}\) simulated experimental spectrum, can caused switching Teslameter. refers simulated spectrum, default: B.shift = 0 (NOTE: depends B parameter. title: Absolute Quantification of Radicals/Spins — quantify_EPR_Abs

what: Read and Process CW EPR Time Series Experiments — readEPR_Exp_Specs_kin
title: Read and Process CW EPR Time Series Experiments — readEPR_Exp_Specs_kin
text: Reading continuous wave (CW) EPR time series spectral data (recorded e.g. 2D_Field_Delay  experiment "Xenon" acquisition/processing software). Function based readEPR_Exp_Specs  includes automatic time correction CW EPR time.series experiments  (see also correct_time_Exp_Specs description documentation). time series EPR spectra  stored individually (one file per one spectrum, e.g. origin = "Magnettech", ESR5000 [11-0422]),  time series needs loaded readEPR_Exp_Specs_multif. origin = "WinEpr"  time_s column usually possesses form spectrum slices, .e. integer number (0,1,2,...) assigned  recorded spectrum. Therefore, radical kinetic analysis converted time_s  (see argument time.delta.slice).

title: Read and Process CW EPR Time Series Experiments — readEPR_Exp_Specs_kin
code: readEPR_Exp_Specs_kin(   path_to_file,   path_to_dsc_par = NULL,   path_to_ygf = NULL,   time.unit = "s",   time.delta.slice = NULL,   col.names = c("index", "B_G", "time_s", "dIepr_over_dB"),   x.unit = "G",   var2nd.series.id = 3,   origin = "xenon",   qValue = NULL,   ... )

title: Read and Process CW EPR Time Series Experiments — readEPR_Exp_Specs_kin
text: path_to_file Character string, path spectrometer/instrumental file, one following extensions: .txt, .csv, .asc, .DTA .spc, including 2D-experimental (.e. \(Intensity\) vs \(B\) vs \(time\)) EPR data. path can also defined file.path function. path_to_dsc_par Character string, path (can also provided file.path) .DSC/.dsc (origin = "xenon"/origin = "magnettech") .par (origin = "winepr") ASCII text file, including instrumental parameters recorded spectra provided EPR machine. Default: path_to_dsc_par = NULL. latter assignment actually means argument automatically inherits path_to_file, however appropriate extension (.DSC/.dsc .par). words, function looking filename like path_to_file working directory. file exist, ask provide/define right file path. path_to_ygf Character string, path (can also provided file.path) binary .YGF file (origin = "xenon"/origin = "magnettech"), storing values 2nd independent variable spectral series like time, temperature, microwave power, ...etc (different magnetic flux density EPR intensity, see also Details /var2nd.series.id argument description 2D experiments). Default: path_to_ygf = NULL. latter assignment actually means argument automatically inherits path_to_file, however appropriate extension .YGF. words, function looking file name like path_to_file working directory. file exist, automatically grabs values based information provided .DSC/.dsc (origin = "xenon"/origin = "magnettech") .par (origin = "winepr") files (see argument path_to_dsc_par description). order read individual .YGF files just apply readBin function following arguments con = path_to_file ,= "numeric", size = 8, n = file_length / 8, signed = TRUE, endian = "big"/endian = "little", latter depending origin xenon/magnettech, respectively. file_length can calculated readBin(con = path_to_file,= "raw",n = 1e+4) %>% length(). time.unit Character string, specifying "s","min", "h" time.unit = "unitless" (time.delta.slice different NULL). Default: time.unit = "s" time.delta.slice Numeric, time interval time.unit slices, case origin = "winepr". Default: time.delta.slice = NULL (actually, corresponding 1 time.unit). col.names Character string vector, corresponding desired column/variable names/headers returned data frame/table. safe rule thumb use column names incl. physical quantity notation unit, Quantity_Unit like "B_G", "RF_MHz" "Bsim_mT" (e.g. pointing simulated EPR spectrum \(x\)-axis). Default: col.names = c("index","B_G","time_s","dIepr_over_dB") (orgin = "xenon"). spectral 2D-time series col.names must include character string ("time_s") order identify time EPR spectra recorded. x.unit Character string, corresponding original x variable/column unit, "G", "mT" "MHz". var2nd.series.id Numeric index related col.names vector pointing column EPR spectral 2D- time series variable. Default: var2nd.series.id = 3 ("Xenon" time series experiment, corresponding "time" column). origin Character string, corresponding origin data related EPR acquisition software spectrometer (data loaded automatically using default parameters). Options summarized following table (specific origin may added later) => qValue Numeric, Q value (quality sensitivity factor number) displayed specific dB spectrometer, case Xenon new Magnettech software returned automatically, however case WinEPR, must provided user. default: qValue = NULL, actually corresponding value 1. ... additional arguments specified, see also readEPR_Exp_Specs fread.

time series coming from `Magnettech` as individual EPR spectra ## (represented by binary files `.DTA`) recorded at different ## time in seconds -> see `names` argument readEPR_Exp_Specs_multif(   name.pattern = "Kinetics_EPR_Spectra_",   dir_asc_bin = "./Input_EPR_Data",   dir_dsc_par = "./Input_EPR_Data",   read.ascii = FALSE,   names = c("20","40","60","80","100","120"),   tidy = TRUE,   var2nd.series = "time_s",   origin = "magnettech" ) # ## time series coming from `Magnettech` as individual EPR spectra ## (represented by ASCII files `.csv`) recorded at different ## time in seconds -> see `names` argument data.time.series.mngtech <-   readEPR_Exp_Specs_multif(     name.pattern = "Kinetics_EPR_Spectra_",     dir_asc_bin = "./Input_EPR_Data",     dir_dsc_par = "./Input_EPR_Data",     col.names = c("B_mT","dIepr_over_dB"),     x.unit = "mT",     names = as.character(c(1:12)), # total number of spectra: 12     tidy = TRUE,     var2nd.series = "Slice",     origin = "magnettech"   ) # ## convert the `Slice` column (of the previous data) into `time_s`, ## using the `dplyr` package, time interval between recording ## of the two consecutive Slices/EPR spectra corresponds to 32 s: data.time.series.mngtech <-   data.time.series.mngtech %>%     mutate(time_s = (Slice - 1) * 32) # 32 s time interval ## correct time, if the middle of an individual spectrum ## appears at the sweep time half data.time.series.mngtech$time_s <-   correct_time_Exp_Specs(     time.s = data.time.series.mngtech$time_s,     # how many accumulations per individual EPR spectrum ? :     Nscans = 1,     # experimental sweep time (for one EPR spectrum) in seconds:     sweep.time.s = 26    ) # } # }
